mainTopic: Who counts as a פצוע דכא: damage בידי שמים, where the injury must be, the עטרה, and the shape of a cut
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge about a man whose testicle was pierced by a thorn and who still had children. The גמרא answers that רב doubted the children were his. שמואל rules that a man damaged בידי שמים is כשר. This is supported by the word פצוע in the פסוק and by a ברייתא comparing it to ממזר. רבא then teaches that wounded, crushed and severed each apply to the member, the testicles and the cords. The גמרא proves that פצוע דכא means an injury to the private parts: it compares it to כרות שפכה and reads that phrase closely, ruling out the lips and the nose. Next come rules about a hole in the עטרה and how much of the עטרה must remain. רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree about a cut shaped like a quill or a gutter, and the final הלכה is that both shapes are כשר. The amud ends with two real cases. The second one, about seed leaving through the urinary passage, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The man pierced by a thorn who still had children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes telling a real case: a thorn pierced a man's testicle and pus-like fluid came out, yet he later had children.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a thorn pierced him in the testicles, and something like a thread of pus came out of him, and yet he had children!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge that began just before this section. It brings a real story to show that a man with a pierced testicle can still father children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא treated a pierced testicle as damage that makes a man unable to have children, so he counts as a פצוע דכא. This story seems to prove the opposite, because the man had children. If the story holds, a pierced testicle might not be a disqualifying injury at all.

phrases.english: and a thorn pierced him in the testicles,
and something like a thread of pus came out of him,
and yet he had children!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a pierced testicle makes a man sterile and a פצוע דכא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real man with a pierced testicle had children, so the injury did not make him sterile.

steps.title: The children were suspected not to be his
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this very case was sent from שמואל to רב, who said to look into where the children really came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't שמואל send this case before רב, and he said to him: Go and check about his children, where they come from.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The case is no proof, because רב doubted those children were really the man's own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on the children being his. רב's instruction to investigate shows he thought a man with this injury cannot father children, so the wife was suspected of having children from another man. The original rule stands: a pierced testicle is a disqualifying injury.

keyTerms.meaning: Go around and look into, investigate

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying a man like this sometimes has children. He means the children likely belong to another man, so the story proves nothing.

phrases.english: But didn't Shmuel send this case before Rav

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: צֵא וְחָזַר עַל בָּנָיו מֵאֵין הֵם.
phrases.english: and he said to him: Go and check about his children, where they come from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Undermines the factual basis of the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man with the pierced testicle fathered the children, so the injury does not make him sterile.
steps.terutzMaskana: The children were suspected to be from another man. The injury does make him sterile, and the rule stands.

steps.title: Damage from Heaven does not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that a man who is a פצוע דכא בידי שמים is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A man with crushed testicles by the hand of Heaven is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule begins here. רב יהודה quotes שמואל: if the damage came from Heaven and not from a person, the man is not disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a פצוע דכא marrying into the community covers damage that was caused, like an injury. A man born this way, or damaged by illness, is outside the ban and may marry a woman born Jewish. This limits the law to injuries done by people.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with wounded or crushed testicles, who may not marry into the community
By the hand of Heaven: from birth or illness, not caused by a person
Fit, allowed (here: to marry into the community)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule: only damage caused by a person makes a man a פצוע דכא who may not marry into the community.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
One with crushed testicles by the hand of Heaven is fit.
phrases.notes: 'By the hand of Heaven' means he was born like this or it came from an illness, not from someone hurting him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about the type of damage that disqualifies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פצוע דכא whose condition is בידי שמים is כשר to marry into the community.

steps.title: רבא: the exact word in the verse shows it
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that שמואל's rule fits the wording of the פסוק, which says פצוע and not הפצוע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: That is why we read 'wounded' and we do not read 'the wounded one'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings support for שמואל's rule from the exact word the תורה uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פצוע suggests someone who got wounded, meaning something happened to him. The form הפצוע could have meant anyone in this condition, even from birth. Because the תורה chose פצוע, the ban covers only injury, which fits שמואל.

phrases.english: Rava said: That is why we read "wounded,"
phrases.notes: דברים 23:2

phrases.english: and we do not read "the wounded one."
phrases.notes: The word the תורה uses points to someone who got hurt, not someone who was always this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from the פסוק for שמואל's rule in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that damage בידי שמים does not disqualify
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording פצוע rather than הפצוע in דברים 23:2

steps.title: A ברייתא compares to the ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא links the פסוק of פצוע to the next פסוק about a ממזר. Just as a ממזר is made by people, so is the disqualifying injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: It says 'A wounded one shall not enter,' and it says 'A ממזר shall not enter.' Just as there it comes from the hands of man, so too here it comes from the hands of man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second support for שמואל, this time from a ברייתא that compares two פסוקים standing next to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the same words, לא יבא, so the ברייתא learns one from the other. A ממזר's problem comes from what people did, since his parents sinned. So the פצוע of the first פסוק must also be someone injured by a person, not born that way.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A child born from a forbidden union, who may not marry into the community
Just as there, so too here (a comparison between two cases)
By the hands of man, caused by people

steps.whatToRemember: Two supports back שמואל: the word פצוע (רבא) and the comparison to ממזר (the ברייתא). Both show that only damage caused by a person disqualifies.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
It says: "A wounded one shall not enter,"
phrases.notes: דברים 23:2

phrases.english: and it says: "A mamzer shall not enter."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:3, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: Just as there it is by the hands of man,
phrases.notes: "There" is the ממזר, whose problem comes from what his parents did.

phrases.english: so too here it is by the hands of man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate source for the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that only damage בידי אדם disqualifies
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing פצוע (דברים 23:2) to ממזר (דברים 23:3)

steps.title: רבא: each type of injury applies to each body part
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that each of the three words, פצוע, דך and כרות, applies to each of three parts: the member, the testicles, and the spermatic cords.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'Wounded' applies to all of them, 'crushed' applies to all of them, 'severed' applies to all of them. Wounded applies to all: whether the member, the testicles, or the spermatic cords were wounded. Crushed applies to all: whether the member, the testicles, or the spermatic cords were crushed. Severed applies to all: whether the member, the testicles, or the spermatic cords were severed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new teaching that maps out which injuries count. He states a short rule, then spells it out piece by piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names three injuries: פצוע (wounded), דכא (crushed) and כרות (severed). One might think each word goes with only one body part. רבא says no: any of the three injuries to any of the three parts disqualifies, which makes nine cases in all.

keyTerms.meaning: In all of them, applies to all the parts

steps.whatToRemember: Three injuries (wounded, crushed, severed) times three parts (member, testicles, cords) equals nine ways to be disqualified, as long as a person caused it.

phrases.english: Rava said: "Wounded" applies to all of them,
"crushed" applies to all of them,
"severed" applies to all of them.
Wounded applies to all of them:
whether the member was wounded,
or the testicles were wounded,
or the spermatic cords were wounded.
Crushed applies to all of them:
whether the member was crushed,
or the testicles were crushed,
or the spermatic cords were crushed.
Severed applies to all of them:
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets. It's added so this line matches the two lines before it.

phrases.english: whether the member was severed,
or the testicles were severed,
or the spermatic cords were severed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what causes the damage to which kinds of damage count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the three injuries in the פסוק (פצוע, דך, כרות) disqualifies whether it is to the member, the testicles, or the spermatic cords.

steps.title: How do we know the injury is in the private parts?
steps.stepSummary: One of the חכמים asks רבא how we know that פצוע דכא refers to an injury in the private parts. Perhaps it means an injury to the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the חכמים said to רבא: How do we know that this פצוע דכא means an injury 'in that place'? Maybe it means an injury to his head!
steps.whatsHappening: A student asks רבא what proves that the פסוק of פצוע דכא is talking about the private parts. After all, the words could also describe a head injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words פצוע דכא literally mean 'wounded by crushing,' and they do not say where the wound is. The student wants a source for the place of the injury. This is a real request for information, not an attack on any earlier ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
In 'that place': a polite way of saying the private parts

phrases.english: One of the Rabbis said to Rava:
From where do we know that this 'petzua dakka'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in דברים 23:2.

phrases.english: is an injury in that place?
Say that it means an injury on his head!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּהַאי פְּצוּעַ דַּכָּא בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Earlier steps assumed the injury is in the private parts. Now the גמרא asks for the source of that assumption.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that פצוע דכא refers to an injury to the private parts and not to the head.

steps.title: רבא: no generations are counted for him
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the תורה does not count generations for a פצוע דכא. This shows the injury is one that stops him from having children, so it must be in the private parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since the פסוק does not count generations for him, learn from this that it means an injury in that place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a proof from what the פסוק leaves out: it never mentions this man's descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a ממזר and for an עמוני or מואבי, the תורה mentions generations of descendants. For a פצוע דכא it mentions none. רבא reads this to mean the man cannot have children at all, and that only makes sense if the injury is in the private parts.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִדְּלָא מְנָה בֵּיהּ דּוֹרוֹת,
phrases.english: He said to him: From the fact that it does not count generations for him,
phrases.notes: Unlike the פסוקים about a ממזר or an עמוני, which mention his descendants.

phrases.english: learn from this that it is in that place.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּלָא מְנָה בֵּיהּ דּוֹרוֹת שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק counts no generations for him, so he cannot have children, so the injury must be in the private parts.

steps.title: Maybe only he is forbidden, not his children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the תורה counts no generations because only the man himself is forbidden, while his son and grandson are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the reason the פסוק does not count generations is that only he himself is forbidden, while his son and his son's son are כשר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's proof by offering another reason why the פסוק might not mention generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא understood the missing generations as a fact about the body: he cannot have children. The גמרא suggests it could be a rule of הלכה instead: the איסור applies only to him and does not pass to his children. If that is the reason, the proof that the injury is in the private parts falls apart.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא הַאי דְּלָא מָנָה בּוֹ דּוֹרוֹת,
phrases.english: But perhaps this, that it does not count generations for him,
is because he alone is forbidden,
while his son and his son's son are fit?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הַאי דְּלָא מָנָה בּוֹ דּוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's proof from the missing generations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The missing generations could mean the איסור does not pass to his children, not that he cannot have children.

steps.title: A new proof: it is like כרות שפכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the point a different way. פצוע דכא appears together with כרות שפכה, and just as כרות שפכה is an injury in the private parts, so is פצוע דכא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is similar to כרות שפכה: just as כרות שפכה is an injury in that place, so too this one is in that place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the rejected proof with a new one. It compares פצוע דכא to כרות שפכה, which appears in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof no longer depends on the missing generations. Since the two cases sit side by side in one פסוק, they are read the same way. כרות שפכה is clearly about the private parts, so פצוע דכא is too.

keyTerms.meaning: One whose member is cut off (literally 'cut at the pouring')

phrases.english: It is similar to 'kerut shofkha':
phrases.notes: Both are in the same פסוק, דברים 23:2.

phrases.english: just as kerut shofkha is in that place,
so too, this one is also in that place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the question of step 7 after step 9 weakened רבא's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement proof from the neighboring case in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source was the missing generations, which step 9 showed could be explained another way.
steps.terutzMaskana: פצוע דכא is learned from כרות שפכה: both are injuries to the private parts.

steps.title: How do we know כרות שפכה itself is in the private parts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that כרות שפכה refers to the private parts. Maybe it means a cut to the lips.
steps.simpleTranslation: And כרות שפכה itself, how do we know it is in that place? Say it means his lips!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new proof by asking whether its base, כרות שפכה, is really about the private parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 10 only works if כרות שפכה is clearly about the private parts. The גמרא suggests it could mean the lips, the place spit comes out of. If so, the comparison would prove nothing about the private parts.

phrases.english: And kerut shofkha itself,
from where do we know that it is in that place?
Say it means from his lips!
phrases.notes: The lips are also a place things come out from, namely spit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְרוּת שׇׁפְכָה גּוּפֵיהּ מִמַּאי דִּבְאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the base of the comparison made in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that כרות שפכה refers to the private parts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If כרות שפכה could mean the lips, comparing פצוע דכא to it proves nothing about the private parts.

steps.title: The word שפכה means a place that pours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word שפכה means 'pouring.' That describes the private parts, which pour out, and not the lips.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'שפכה': a place that pours out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the exact word in the פסוק: שפכה comes from 'pouring.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring describes the private parts, not the lips, from which spit is spat. This rules out the lips, but the next step asks whether the nose, which also pours, could fit. Step 14 answers that.
steps.whatToRemember: פצוע דכא and כרות שפכה both refer to injuries to the private parts. This is learned by comparing the two cases in the same פסוק, and from the word שפכה, which means 'pouring.'

phrases.english: 'Shofkha' is written,
meaning in a place that pours out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 and so secures the proof of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כרות שפכה might mean the lips.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word שפכה means pouring, which fits only the private parts.

steps.title: Maybe It Means the Nose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שפכה might refer to the nose, since the nose also 'pours.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means a cut to his nose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepted that 'pouring' rules out the lips. Now it asks: the nose also pours out mucus, so maybe כרות שפכה means a cut nose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 12 depended on the meaning 'pouring.' The nose also discharges liquid, so the 'pouring' definition alone does not prove we are talking about the private parts.

phrases.english: But say it means from his nose!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'pouring' answer of Step 12 by offering another organ that pours.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שפכה can only describe the private parts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The nose also pours out liquid, so the word 'pouring' fits the nose too.

steps.title: Pouring Only Because of the Cut
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means something that pours only because it was cut. The nose pours either way, so it is ruled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it say 'in pouring'? It says 'cut, pouring.' That means something that pours because it was cut. Without a cut, it does not pour; it shoots out. This rules out the nose, which pours whether it is cut or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the two words together. The פסוק describes an organ that pours only as a result of the cut, and that only fits the private parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only meant 'something that pours,' the nose would fit. But 'כרות שפכה' ties the pouring to the cut. Normally semen shoots out, and it only dribbles after a cut. The nose pours in both cases, so the cut changes nothing there.

keyTerms.meaning: This way and that way (either case)

steps.whatToRemember: כרות שפכה means a cut in the private parts that changes how semen comes out. This is the source that both פצוע דכא and כרות שפכה are injuries in that place.

phrases.english: Is it written 'in pouring'?!
phrases.notes: That wording would mean anything that pours, with no link to a cut.

phrases.english: It is written 'cut, pouring'
meaning something that pours out because of a cut,
but when there is no cut
it does not pour out; it shoots out.
This excludes that one (the nose),
since either way, cut or not, it pours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the nose challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שפכה just means 'pouring,' so the nose could fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pouring must be caused by the cut, which fits only the private parts.

steps.title: A ברייתא Links פצוע דכא to ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves that פצוע דכא is in the private parts by comparing it to ממזר, which uses the same phrase 'shall not enter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: It says 'A פצוע דכא shall not enter,' and it says 'A ממזר shall not enter.' Just as there it is about that place, so too here it is about that place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another proof for the same idea. The proof uses the shared wording 'לא יבא' in two nearby פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזר comes from a forbidden relationship, so his status is tied to 'that place,' the private parts. Because the תורה uses the same words for פצוע דכא, the ברייתא learns that his injury is also in that place.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A child born from a forbidden relationship
Just as there, so too here

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: It says:
'A פצוע דכא shall not enter,'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:2

phrases.english: and it says: 'A ממזר shall not enter.'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:3

phrases.english: Just as there it is about that place,
so too here it is about that place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another source, from a ברייתא, for the conclusion reached in Steps 10–14.
steps.raayaObject: That פצוע דכא is an injury in the private parts
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared phrase 'לא יבא' used for both פצוע דכא and ממזר

steps.title: A Hole Partly Through the עטרה
steps.stepSummary: In a case where a hole starts below the עטרה on one side and comes out above it on the other side, רבי חייא בר אבא wanted to rule him כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was pierced below the עטרה, and the opposite side of the hole was above the עטרה, רבי חייא בר אבא thought to rule him כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new practical case about a hole through the organ. רבי חייא בר אבא gives his first opinion, and that opinion sets up the response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since one end of the hole is outside the area that would make him פסול, רבי חייא בר אבא thought the damage does not count. This is only his initial view (סבר), and it gets challenged right away.

keyTerms.meaning: The corona (crown-shaped edge) of the organ

phrases.english: If it was pierced below the עטרה,
phrases.notes: "Below" here means at the עטרה itself, on one side.

phrases.english: and its opposite end was above the עטרה,

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְאַכְשׁוֹרֵי.
phrases.english: רבי חייא בר אבא thought to rule him כשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source of the law to a practical case of a pierced organ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא בר אבא initially holds that a hole partly outside the dangerous area leaves him כשר.

steps.title: Any Damage to the עטרה Makes Him פסול
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי: any hole in the עטרה, of any size, makes him פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said to him: This is what רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The עטרה, any amount, holds him back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי pushes back on רבי חייא בר אבא by quoting a rule from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the hole passes through the עטרה, it counts as damage there, even if one end is elsewhere. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that even a small amount of damage to the עטרה makes him פסול, so רבי חייא בר אבא's idea is rejected.

phrases.english: רבי אסי said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: This is what רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
The עטרה, any amount of damage there, makes him פסול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי חייא בר אבא's initial ruling in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the כשר ruling for a hole that is partly in the עטרה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Any damage to the עטרה, even a little, makes him פסול, so having one end outside does not help.

steps.title: How Much of the עטרה Must Remain
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks about the משנה's 'hair's-breadth' of עטרה that must remain: must it go all the way around, or around most of it?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If some of the עטרה remained...' רבינא sat and asked: The hair's-breadth they spoke of, must it go across all of it or across most of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and then brings רבינא's question about what that line means exactly. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if a hair's-breadth of the עטרה is left, he stays כשר. But it does not say how far around that thin strip has to go. רבינא wants to know if it must circle the whole thing or just the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: A hair's-breadth (the width of a thread)
All of it / most of it

phrases.english: 'And if some of the עטרה remained' etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting only the start of the line from the משנה; the rest says a hair's-breadth is enough.

phrases.english: רבינא sat and asked:
The hair's-breadth that they spoke of,

phrases.aramaic: עַל פְּנֵי כּוּלָּהּ אוֹ עַל פְּנֵי רוּבָּהּ?
phrases.english: must it go across all of it or across most of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to another detail of the עטרה, based on the משנה's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the remaining hair's-breadth of עטרה must go all the way around or only around most of it

steps.title: Around Most of It, Toward the Top
steps.stepSummary: רבא תוספאה answers: the hair's-breadth must go around most of it, and it must be toward the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא תוספאה said to רבינא: The hair's-breadth must go across most of it, and toward the רישא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא תוספאה answers רבינא's question. A majority is enough, and he adds where that strip must be located.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He picks the easier choice: the strip does not need to go all the way around, only most of the way. He also adds a new condition that רבינא did not ask about: the strip must be toward the רישא, the side closer to the body.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers רבינא here

steps.whatToRemember: Even a tiny hole in the עטרה makes him פסול. But if a hair's-breadth of the עטרה remains around most of it, toward the רישא, he stays כשר.

phrases.english: רבא תוספאה said to רבינא:
The hair's-breadth must go across most of it,
and toward the head.
phrases.notes: Here this means the part closer to the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Most of the way around is enough, as long as the strip is toward the רישא.

steps.title: רב הונא: A quill-shaped cut is fit, a gutter-shaped cut is unfit
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a cut shaped like a קולמוס is כשר and one shaped like a מרזב is פסול, because air reaches inside the gutter-shaped cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: if it was cut like a quill, he is כשר. If it was cut like a gutter, he is פסול. In the gutter case the air gets in; in the quill case the air does not get in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new rule about two shapes of a cut, and he explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A quill-shaped cut is closed and pointed all around. A gutter-shaped cut is open on one side, like a half-pipe. רב הונא's concern is air: when air reaches the open gutter-shaped cut, it harms the flow of seed.

keyTerms.meaning: A quill pen, cut to a point that slopes evenly on all sides
A gutter, open along one side
The air reaches it and has an effect on it

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
If cut like a quill, he is fit;
phrases.notes: A quill is cut to a point, sloping evenly all around.

phrases.english: if cut like a gutter, he is unfit.
phrases.notes: A gutter is open along one side, like a half-pipe.

phrases.english: In this one, the air gets at it,
and in this one, the air does not get at it.
phrases.notes: The first 'this one' is the gutter cut; the second is the quill cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כְּקוּלְמוֹס — כְּשֵׁרָה, כְּמַרְזֵב — פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the hole and hair's-breadth cases to a new question: what shape the cut has.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A quill-shaped cut is כשר and a gutter-shaped cut is פסול, because air reaches the open gutter shape.

steps.title: רב חסדא: The reverse, because of rubbing
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the opposite: the gutter shape is כשר and the quill shape is פסול, because only the gutter shape rubs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: if it was cut like a gutter, he is כשר. If it was cut like a quill, he is פסול. The gutter shape rubs; the quill shape does not rub.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא disagrees with רב הונא and flips the ruling, giving his own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא is looking at a different concern. He does not focus on air. He focuses on whether the organ rubs during relations. A quill shape is too thin and pointed to rub, so in his view that shape is the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who argues with רב הונא here

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
If cut like a gutter, he is fit;
if cut like a quill, he is unfit!
This one rubs,
and this one does not rub.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: כְּמַרְזֵב כְּשֵׁרָה, כְּקוּלְמוֹס פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite ruling from רב הונא's, based on a different concern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gutter-shaped cut is כשר and a quill-shaped cut is פסול, because only the gutter shape rubs.

steps.title: רבא sides with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב הונא's view makes more sense, because the air concern is real.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it makes sense to follow רב הונא. In the quill case the air does not get in, and in the gutter case the air does get in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא decides between the two opinions and picks רב הונא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא accepts that the air concern is real. On that basis, the quill shape is better than the gutter shape. His next step will deal with רב חסדא's rubbing argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Like him (in agreement with his view)
It makes sense / it stands to reason

phrases.english: Rava said:
It makes sense to follow Rav Huna.
In this one, the air does not get at it,
and in this one, the air does get at it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument from Steps 20 and 21 in favor of רב הונא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא agrees with רב הונא: the air concern makes the gutter shape the problem.

steps.title: רבא answers the rubbing argument with a barrel stopper
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רב חסדא's concern: a quill shape can still make contact, just like a pointed barrel stopper.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you are worried about rubbing, it is just like the stopper of a barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes away רב חסדא's reason for calling the quill shape פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A barrel stopper is pointed at one end, but its wider part still presses against the sides and seals the hole. In the same way, the quill-shaped organ still makes enough contact higher up. So רב חסדא's rubbing worry does not apply.

phrases.english: And if it is because of rubbing,
it is just like the stopper of a barrel.
phrases.notes: A stopper is pointed at the tip, yet its wider part still seals the hole tightly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם גְּרִידוּתָא — מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַבַּרְזָא דְחָבִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's support for רב הונא by answering רב חסדא's reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב חסדא's reason for calling the quill shape פסול
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A pointed shape still makes enough contact, just as a pointed barrel stopper still seals.

steps.title: The הלכה: both shapes are fit
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells מרימר that מר זוטרא, quoting רב פפא, ruled that both the quill shape and the gutter shape are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to מרימר: this is what מר זוטרא said in the name of רב פפא. The הלכה is that whether it was cut like a quill or like a gutter, he is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A final הלכה is reported, and it goes further than both opinions: neither shape makes him פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling sets aside both רב הונא's air concern and רב חסדא's rubbing concern as reasons to call someone פסול. Both cut shapes are כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a cut shaped like a קולמוס and a cut shaped like a מרזב are both כשר.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Mareimar:
This is what Mar Zutra said
in the name of Rav Pappa:
The halacha is: whether like a quill
or like a gutter, he is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְמָרִימָר, הָכִי אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical הלכה, and it goes beyond both opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both a quill-shaped cut and a gutter-shaped cut are כשר.

steps.title: Where on the organ is this cut?
steps.stepSummary: A question is raised: is this cut below the עטרה or above it?
steps.simpleTranslation: However, he asked: is this talking about a cut below the עטרה, or above it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about where on the organ the cut in this ruling is, and sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that both shapes are כשר only makes sense once we know where the cut is. 'Below' means on the end side, at the עטרה itself. 'Above' means further up, closer to the body.

keyTerms.meaning: He had a question / it was unclear to him
Below the עטרה (on the end side)

phrases.english: However, he had a question:
Below the corona, or above?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיהוּ, מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: לְמַטָּה מֵעֲטָרָה, אוֹ לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where the cut in the halacha of Step 24 is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the quill or gutter cut below the עטרה or above it?

steps.title: Obviously it means above the corona
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it must mean above the עטרה. Below it, even a complete cut-off would be כשר, so the shape of the cut would not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that it means above the עטרה. If you thought it meant below the עטרה, then even if the organ were cut off completely he would also be כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that one of the two options makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already says that if a hair's-breadth of the עטרה remains, he is כשר even when the end is cut off. So there would be nothing new in saying a shaped cut there is כשר. The ruling must be about a cut higher up, where we would otherwise worry.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: It is obvious that it means above the corona,
for if you think it means below the corona,
then even if the organ were cut off, he would also be fit.
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה: if a hair's-breadth of the עטרה remains, he is כשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא דִּלְמַעְלָה מֵעֲטָרָה, דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לְמַטָּה מֵעֲטָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cut is above the עטרה. Below it, even a full cut-off is כשר, so the ruling would teach nothing new.

steps.title: רבינא was only testing מרימר
steps.stepSummary: If the answer is obvious, why did רבינא ask? He was trying to trip up מרימר and test him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבינא only wanted to trip up מרימר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a question with an obvious answer was asked at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a hidden question here: why would רבינא ask something so obvious? The answer is that he asked on purpose, to see whether מרימר would get confused.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבינא really did not know the answer. The גמרא says his question was only a test.

phrases.english: And Ravina, to trip up Mareimar,
is what he wanted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the question in Step 25 was asked even though Step 26 showed it was obvious.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבינא really did not know the answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: He knew it, and asked only to test מרימר.

steps.title: A real case in מתא מחסיא: trimmed into a quill shape
steps.stepSummary: In מתא מחסיא, מר בר רב אשי trimmed a man's cut into a quill shape and ruled him כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case in מתא מחסיא. מר בר רב אשי trimmed it evenly like a quill and ruled him כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where the quill-shape rule was put into practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gemara does not say why he trimmed it. A quill shape is כשר even according to רב הונא, while the הלכה in Step 24 accepts both shapes. The cut was made into a quill shape so that the man would clearly be כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: He smoothed it / trimmed it evenly

phrases.english: There was a certain case
that happened in Mata Mechasya.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁפְּיֵיהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי כְּקוּלְמוֹס
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi trimmed it evenly like a quill
and ruled him fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the quill-shape ruling being used in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cut trimmed into a quill shape is כשר.

steps.title: A real case in פומבדיתא: seed exits the urinary passage
steps.stepSummary: In פומבדיתא, a man's seed passage was blocked and his seed came out through the urinary passage. רב ביבי בר אביי wanted to rule him כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case in פומבדיתא. The passage for seed became blocked, and the seed came out through the urinary passage. רב ביבי בר אביי thought to rule him כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new real case, and one rabbi leans toward ruling the man כשר. This sets up the pushback that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing here was crushed or cut off, so רב ביבי בר אביי thought the man was כשר. The question is whether seed coming out through the wrong passage makes him פסול.

phrases.english: There was a certain case that happened in Pumbedita.
The passage for seed became blocked,
and he released it through the urinary passage.

phrases.aramaic: סְבַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי לְאַכְשׁוֹרֵי.
phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye thought to rule him fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second real case, about a different kind of injury.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ביבי בר אביי leaned toward ruling the man כשר.

steps.title: רב פפי begins to push back
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי starts to object to ruling the man כשר. His words continue on the next daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: because you come from...
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי begins to challenge רב ביבי בר אביי's leaning, but his sentence finishes on the next daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'because you come' sound like an attack on רב ביבי's background or reasoning. The full content of the pushback only appears in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who pushes back against רב ביבי

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said: Because you come
phrases.notes: His sentence continues on the next daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to challenge רב ביבי בר אביי's leaning toward כשר in Step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב ביבי בר אביי's leaning to rule the man כשר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated; the objection continues on the next daf.
